label: ACME CFI-G
title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
tier_reason: Team list, Tier 2. PSI subarea: Flames of Gaseous Fuels.

summary_student.text: Gas fuels such as propane, butane and pentane were burned from small ball-shaped burners aboard the International Space Station to make 'cool flames', which burn much colder than ordinary flames. The goal was to learn when these cool flames appear, go out, or turn into hot flames. The record links the work to more efficient car engines and does not state a fire-safety use.

summary_professional.text: Spherical gas-fueled diffusion flames of propane, n-butane and n-pentane were burned on porous spherical burners in the ACME hardware of the Combustion Integrated Rack aboard the ISS, in both normal and inverse configurations. Reactant dilution, fluent flow rate and pressure were varied to determine the conditions for steady cool diffusion flames across a broad range of Zst and Tad, including extinction and transition to hot flames. Flames were observed with cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes and thermocouples, and the data support CFD simulations and the development of a chemical kinetics mechanism.

pillar.reason: The record states no fire-safety use; its stated impact is testing cool-flame kinetics mechanisms to help develop more efficient internal combustion engines.

environments.reason: The flame tests were performed aboard the International Space Station.
